name: Data Validation & Quality
description: Controls that keep critical data accurate, complete, timely and traceable, from source capture and ingestion through transformation and reconciliation to reporting. Suited to finance, regulatory reporting and analytics pipelines.
references: DAMA-DMBOK 2, BCBS 239, ISO 8000, SOX key reports (IPE), SOC 2 Processing Integrity

categories.name: Data Governance & Ownership
categories.objective: Critical data has accountable owners, agreed definitions and lifecycle rules.

items.control: A data governance policy and council define data domains, decision rights and escalation for data issues.
items.risk: Data issues stall because no one has authority to resolve them.
items.test: Inspect the policy for approval within 12 months, and council minutes for decisions and escalations.

items.control: Critical data elements (CDEs) are identified by their impact on financial, regulatory and customer outcomes, and each has a named owner and steward.
items.risk: Quality effort is spread thin and nobody is accountable for the data that matters most.
items.test: Inspect the CDE register and selection criteria, and confirm owners and stewards are current for a sample of CDEs.
evidence: CDE register with owner, steward and criticality

items.control: A business glossary and data dictionary define each CDE's meaning, format, valid values and system of record.
items.risk: Teams interpret the same field differently, producing inconsistent figures.
items.test: For sampled CDEs, confirm the glossary entry is complete and matches the physical column definition in the system of record.
evidence: Business glossary entries (e.g. Collibra, Alation, Purview)

items.control: Datasets are classified for confidentiality and criticality in the data catalogue, and handling rules follow from the classification.
items.risk: Sensitive data is handled with the wrong level of protection.
items.test: For a sample of catalogued datasets, confirm a classification label is applied and matches the content.

items.control: Retention and disposal rules are applied to datasets and enforced by automated deletion or archiving.
items.risk: Data is kept longer than permitted, or deleted before legal retention ends.
items.test: For sampled datasets, compare the configured retention to the schedule and inspect deletion job logs.
evidence: Lifecycle or retention configuration on data stores

categories.name: Data Quality Rules & Thresholds
categories.objective: Data quality expectations are explicit, measurable and agreed with consumers.

items.control: Each CDE has measurable data quality rules across the relevant dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity and uniqueness.
items.risk: Quality cannot be measured, so problems are found only by downstream users.
items.test: For sampled CDEs, confirm rules exist for each relevant dimension and are implemented in the DQ tool.
evidence: DQ rule catalogue mapped to CDEs and dimensions
Rule implementation in the DQ tool (e.g. dbt tests, Great Expectations, Informatica DQ)

items.control: Data quality thresholds (e.g. at least 99.5% completeness) are agreed with consumers and recorded in data contracts or SLAs.
items.risk: Producers and consumers disagree on what good enough means.
items.test: Inspect data contracts or SLAs for sampled CDEs and confirm thresholds are signed off by the consuming function.
evidence: Data contracts or SLAs with thresholds
Threshold configuration in the DQ tool

items.control: Data contracts between producers and consumers define schema, semantics, SLAs and change-notice periods, enforced through a schema registry.
items.risk: Upstream schema changes break downstream pipelines without warning.
items.test: Inspect sampled data contracts and confirm schema registry compatibility checks block breaking changes.

items.control: New sources are profiled before onboarding to set baselines and detect anomalies.
items.risk: Poor-quality sources are onboarded and contaminate downstream data.
items.test: For sources onboarded in the period, confirm a profiling report was reviewed before production use.
evidence: Profiling report (null rates, distinct counts, value distributions)

items.control: Data quality scorecards by CDE and domain are reported monthly to the governance council.
items.risk: Deteriorating data quality is not visible to decision-makers.
items.test: Inspect three monthly scorecards and confirm breaches have owners and actions.

categories.name: Input Validation
categories.objective: Only complete, valid and authorised data enters downstream systems.

items.control: Ingestion validates schema, data types, required fields and formats, and non-conforming records are quarantined.
items.risk: Malformed records load and corrupt downstream data.
items.test: Inspect validation configuration, then submit a test file with known defects and confirm defective records are quarantined.
evidence: Validation configuration (e.g. dbt tests, Great Expectations suites)

items.control: Key fields have range, domain and referential-integrity checks (valid codes, dates, amounts, foreign keys).
items.risk: Invalid values such as negative quantities or unknown codes pass into reporting.
items.test: Inspect rule definitions for sampled CDEs and the exception reports for the period.

items.control: File transfers are validated with checksums, record counts, header and trailer control totals and duplicate-file detection.
items.risk: Partial, duplicated or tampered files are processed.
items.test: Inspect transfer logs for control-total validation, and replay a duplicate file in test to confirm it is rejected.

items.control: Manual data entry has field-level validation, mandatory fields and maker-checker approval for critical records.
items.risk: Keying errors or fraudulent entries enter the system unchecked.
items.test: Inspect validation configuration and, for a sample of critical entries, confirm a different user approved them.

items.control: Duplicate records are detected at ingestion using business keys or fuzzy matching.
items.risk: Duplicates inflate counts, balances or customer numbers.
items.test: Inspect deduplication logic and run a duplicate query on a key table to confirm the rate is within threshold.

items.control: Rejected records are tracked, corrected at source and reprocessed with an audit trail.
items.risk: Rejected data is silently lost, leaving reporting incomplete.
items.test: Inspect the rejection queue ageing and, for a sample, trace correction and successful reprocessing.

categories.name: Processing & Transformation
categories.objective: Data is transformed completely and accurately, only through reviewed and tested logic.

items.control: Transformation logic is documented, traceable to business requirements and peer-reviewed.
items.risk: Logic errors silently miscalculate figures.
items.test: For sampled transformations, trace logic to the specification and confirm an independent reviewer approved the code.

items.control: Pipelines have automated unit tests on transformations and regression tests on outputs that must pass in CI.
items.risk: Changes break existing logic without anyone noticing.
items.test: Inspect CI configuration requiring tests to pass, and test results for sampled merges.
evidence: CI configuration with required test step

items.control: Jobs are idempotent with checkpoints, and partial loads are rolled back rather than committed.
items.risk: Reruns double-count data, or failed jobs leave tables half-loaded.
items.test: Inspect orchestration retries and transactional load settings, and re-run a job in test to confirm totals do not change.
evidence: Orchestration configuration (e.g. Airflow, Dagster retries and transactional writes)

items.control: Key calculations and aggregations are independently recalculated or validated by someone outside the build team.
items.risk: Material calculation errors reach financial or regulatory reports.
items.test: Re-perform a sample of key calculations and compare to system output within tolerance.

items.control: Critical tables have integrity protections: database constraints, audit columns and tamper-evident change history.
items.risk: Data is altered without a trace.
items.test: Inspect schema constraints and audit configuration, and trace a sampled change through the audit history.
evidence: Audit trail configuration (e.g. CDC, temporal tables)

categories.name: Reconciliation & Completeness
categories.objective: Data is complete end to end, and breaks are investigated and resolved promptly.

items.control: Each critical load is reconciled source to target on record counts and control totals.
items.risk: Records are dropped or duplicated between systems.
items.test: For a sample of days, inspect reconciliation results and confirm breaks were investigated.

items.control: Reconciliation breaks are investigated within a defined SLA, and aged breaks are escalated.
items.risk: Breaks accumulate and mask real errors.
items.test: Inspect break ageing and confirm breaks older than the SLA were escalated.

items.control: Subledger-to-ledger and system-to-system reconciliations are prepared and reviewed at each period end.
items.risk: Misstatements in the general ledger go undetected.
items.test: For sampled period-end reconciliations, confirm timely preparation, independent review and resolution of reconciling items.

items.control: Completeness is checked against authoritative sources (e.g. every entity, branch or feed has reported).
items.risk: Missing entities or feeds go unnoticed and totals are understated.
items.test: Inspect the completeness check configuration and results for a sample of days.

items.control: Reconciliation rules, tolerances and any auto-cleared or suppressed breaks are reviewed and approved.
items.risk: Overly broad tolerances or suppressions hide genuine errors.
items.test: Inspect the tolerance and suppression list and confirm quarterly approval with rationale.

items.control: Reconciliations are reviewed by someone independent of the preparer.
items.risk: Preparer errors or manipulation go unchallenged.
items.test: For sampled reconciliations, confirm the reviewer differs from the preparer and has appropriate seniority.

categories.name: Master & Reference Data
categories.objective: Master and reference data are authoritative, consistent and protected from unauthorised change.

items.control: Changes to sensitive master data (vendor bank details, customer credit limits) need maker-checker approval and independent call-back verification.
items.risk: Fraudulent changes divert payments or expose the organisation to credit losses.
items.test: From the change log, select vendor bank detail changes and confirm a separate approver and call-back to a number already on file.

items.control: Master data management produces a golden record using documented match, merge and survivorship rules.
items.risk: Duplicate or conflicting master records produce inconsistent reporting.
items.test: Inspect match and survivorship rules and review a sample of merged records for correctness.

items.control: Reference data (code lists, FX rates, hierarchies) is loaded from authoritative sources with effective dating.
items.risk: Stale or incorrect reference values corrupt calculations.
items.test: Compare a sample of loaded reference values (e.g. FX rates) to the authoritative source for the same effective date.

items.control: Master data is checked for cross-system consistency (e.g. CRM against ERP), and inactive or duplicate records are cleansed.
items.risk: Inconsistent master data across systems drives errors and rework.
items.test: Inspect the consistency and cleansing reports for the period and confirm mismatches were resolved.

categories.name: Access Control
categories.objective: Only authorised people and services can change data and data pipelines.

items.control: Write access to production data stores and pipelines is restricted to named roles and reviewed quarterly.
items.risk: Unauthorised users alter production data or pipeline logic.
items.test: Obtain write-privileged users on the warehouse and orchestration tool and confirm quarterly review with removals actioned.
evidence: Write-privilege export (e.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks grants)

items.control: Direct production data fixes require a ticket, approval and a logged script.
items.risk: Ad hoc data fixes introduce errors or conceal fraud.
items.test: Compare database audit logs of direct DML to data-fix tickets and confirm each fix was approved.

items.control: Pipeline service accounts use least privilege and vaulted, rotated credentials.
items.risk: Compromised pipeline credentials expose or alter large volumes of data.
items.test: Inspect grants for pipeline service accounts and confirm credentials are stored in a vault with rotation.

items.control: Sensitive columns are masked or tokenised for analytics users who do not need clear values.
items.risk: Analysts see personal or confidential data they do not need.
items.test: Query a sensitive column as an analytics role and confirm values are masked.
evidence: Query results as an analytics role

categories.name: Change Management
categories.objective: Changes to pipelines, rules and mappings are tested, approved and traceable.

items.control: Pipeline changes go through change management with test evidence and approval before production.
items.risk: Untested pipeline changes corrupt reported figures.
items.test: For 25 sampled pipeline deployments, confirm a change record with test evidence and approval before deployment.
evidence: Change tickets or pull requests with approvals

items.control: Data quality rules and thresholds are version-controlled, and changes are approved by the data steward.
items.risk: Rules are loosened to hide failures.
items.test: Inspect rule change history and confirm steward approval for changes that relax thresholds.

items.control: Mapping and hierarchy tables (chart of accounts, product mappings) are change-controlled and reviewed.
items.risk: Incorrect mappings misclassify amounts in reports.
items.test: For sampled mapping changes, confirm request, approval and post-change review.

items.control: Report and query logic used as key evidence (IPE) is locked down, and changes are approved and tested.
items.risk: Changed report logic produces incomplete or inaccurate key reports relied on by controls.
items.test: Inspect the key report inventory and, for changed reports, confirm approval and testing of completeness and accuracy.
evidence: Report change approvals and test results

categories.name: Monitoring & Issue Management
categories.objective: Data quality issues are detected early, fixed at source, communicated and prevented from recurring.

items.control: Automated data observability monitors volume, schema, freshness and distribution anomalies and alerts owners.
items.risk: Silent data failures reach reports and decisions.
items.test: Inspect monitor coverage of CDE tables and alert history, and confirm alerts were triaged.
evidence: Observability monitor configuration (e.g. Monte Carlo, Soda, Bigeye)

items.control: Late or missing feeds are detected against expected schedules with freshness SLAs.
items.risk: Decisions are made on stale data.
items.test: Inspect freshness SLA configuration for sampled feeds and alert history.

items.control: A DQ issue log records severity, root cause, owner and target date, and fixes are made at source.
items.risk: Issues are patched downstream and keep recurring.
items.test: For sampled closed issues, confirm a root cause and a fix at source, and check recurrence metrics.

items.control: The impact of DQ incidents on downstream reports, decisions and customers is assessed, and stakeholders are notified.
items.risk: Consumers keep using bad data because they were not told.
items.test: For sampled high-severity DQ incidents, confirm an impact assessment and stakeholder notification.

items.control: Data quality controls are tested periodically by an independent function.
items.risk: DQ controls are assumed to work but have degraded.
items.test: Inspect the test plan and workpapers and confirm findings are tracked.

items.control: Data producers and stewards complete data quality training.
items.risk: Staff do not understand their role in data quality.
items.test: Compare training completion records to the steward and producer list.

categories.name: Reporting & Lineage
categories.objective: Reports are accurate, traceable to source, consistently defined and distributed only to authorised recipients.

items.control: End-to-end lineage from source to report is documented for every CDE.
items.risk: Errors cannot be traced to source and the impact of changes cannot be assessed.
items.test: For sampled CDEs, trace lineage from a report figure back to source and confirm the documented lineage matches.
evidence: Lineage tool output (e.g. Collibra, Purview, dbt docs)

items.control: Reports pass analytical review against variance thresholds before distribution.
items.risk: Anomalous figures are published without challenge.
items.test: For sampled report cycles, confirm variance analysis was performed and large variances were explained before release.

items.control: KPI definitions and calculation methods are documented and applied consistently across reports.
items.risk: Different reports show different numbers for the same KPI.
items.test: Compare a KPI across two or more reports for the same period and confirm values and definitions match.

items.control: Manual adjustments to reported data are documented, approved and tracked.
items.risk: Unsupported top-side adjustments misstate results.
items.test: For all or a sample of adjustments, confirm rationale, support and approval by someone other than the preparer.

items.control: Report distribution is limited to authorised recipients, and sensitive reports are protected.
items.risk: Confidential reports reach unauthorised people.
items.test: Inspect distribution lists and BI workspace permissions for sampled sensitive reports.
evidence: BI workspace permissions (e.g. Power BI, Tableau)
